# Diffusion Planner CAMP Integration V13 Audit

Date: 2026-06-27

This file is the current short-form audit entry point for the CAMP integration
with the fixed TiERIV Diffusion Planner. It replaces v12 for new current-state
writes because the user clarified that broader training data should come from
more fixed-DP candidate-set generation, not from CAMP-generated or modified
trajectories.

## Data Definition And Authorization

The training datum remains a current route/state tick plus the fixed DP
candidate trajectory set for that tick. Expanding data means running the fixed
black-box DP candidate generator on more nonformal route/seed/scenario
combinations. CAMP still only ranks candidate indices by a linear score over
current-tick candidate atoms.


## Larger Fixed DP Candidate Collection Launch

The v13 collection was launched as a queued serial AutoDL job. It waits for the
v12 collection summary before starting so fixed-DP replay does not run
concurrently with the existing v12 replay loop. The v13 pipeline was launched
at the same time and waits for the v13 collection summary before building the
dataset, validating contracts, splitting, fitting train-only scales, running
the sufficiency preflight, and training the offline nonpromotion static CAMP
artifact.

## V13 Default-Off Shadow Selector Implementation

The default-off shadow selector implementation gate was executed after explicit
user authorization for
`dp_camp_v13_default_off_shadow_selector_implementation_only_after_explicit_user_authorization`.
It added a production runner path for a v13 shadow selector that is disabled by
default and fail-closed. When enabled, the runner first checks the immutable
artifact hash contract for the atom scales and static weights/checkpoint. If
the contract is missing or mismatched, candidate count is not K=8, selector
mode is not static, or selector artifact loading fails, the runner does not
install the CAMP predictor and records DP Top-1 fail-closed shadow status in
the summary. If the contract is ready, the runner computes CAMP scores over the
fixed current-tick DP candidate tensor, records `shadow_selected_index`, but
forces `selected_index` and `executed_index` to DP candidate 0. This implements
shadow observability only; it does not route CAMP selection into execution.

This gate did not run replay, generate candidates, train CAMP, modify DP,
promote atoms or selectors, deploy, change the online selector, or authorize
safety/CAMP-over-DP claims.

## V13 Default-Off Shadow Selector Post-Implementation Static Contract Review

The post-implementation static contract review was executed after the actual
default-off shadow selector implementation and focused unit tests were merged
and synchronized to AutoDL. The review inspected the production replay runner,
the focused shadow-selector unit tests, the Benders atom contract tests, and
this v13 audit. It confirmed that the implementation remains default-off,
fail-closed, records only `shadow_selected_index`, forces executed selection to
DP candidate 0 during the shadow phase, preserves fixed-candidate affine
scoring `score_k(w)=a_k^T w`, rejects execution-changing flag combinations,
and keeps promotion/deployment/replay/candidate-generation/DP-modification
boundaries closed.

This gate did not run replay, generate candidates, train CAMP, modify DP,
materialize an artifact manifest, enable the runtime shadow selector, promote
atoms or selectors, deploy, or authorize safety/CAMP-over-DP claims.

## V13 Default-Off Shadow Selector Runtime Artifact Manifest Materializer Implementation

The runtime artifact manifest materializer implementation-only gate added a
default-off, fail-closed materializer script and focused unit tests. The
materializer is designed to read one materialization plan only when explicitly
enabled, verify the expected plan SHA256, verify the fixed DP head, verify the
planned output path, verify `atom_scales` and `static_weights` files and
hashes, and then write exactly one runtime artifact manifest JSON matching the
runner lookup contract. The unit tests exercise this behavior on synthetic
temporary artifacts only.

This implementation gate did not materialize the real runtime manifest, execute
replay, enable the shadow selector, generate candidates, train CAMP, modify DP,
promote atoms or selectors, deploy, or authorize safety/CAMP-over-DP claims.

## V13 Default-Off Shadow Selector Broader Nonformal Shadow Replay Batch Execution

The broader nonformal default-off shadow replay batch executed all 32 preflight
commands on AutoDL at CAMP commit
`aa04ff6cc818d3f2fc44a285a1848ca89d62a355` with fixed DP commit
`7a1d33da277a1992ec474b5383a0c963c72e04e4`. The batch covered four routes
(`sample_normal`, `sample_tl`, `nishi_release`, `nishi_lane_change`), two
non-formal seeds (301, 302), two NPC settings (0, 4), and both traffic-light
modes (`on`, `off`) for 100 replay steps per command.

The validation passed with 32/32 completed commands, 3200 selection records,
3200 shadow records, zero command failures, zero failed shadow records, executed
index always 0, recorded selected index always 0, and shadow scores never routed
to execution. The shadow reranker selected nonzero candidate indices 2505 times,
which confirms the shadow selection path is live while the executed trajectory
remains DP Top-1. This gate did not train CAMP, modify DP, promote a selector,
deploy, or authorize safety/CAMP-over-DP claims.

AutoDL at CAMP commit `d0706908e9d13d28040854776c62fd1885a9c68a` with fixed

v13 base collection and training pipeline, then plans an addon collection over
non-formal seeds 333-364 for the same four routes, two NPC settings, and two
traffic-light modes. The addon is 512 fixed-DP candidate replay commands and

logs and 102400 ticks for fallback-risk retraining.

collection/training scripts and assets exist, DP remains fixed, CAMP remains a
fixed-candidate reranker only, and the Benders score contract remains

does not authorize CAMP candidate generation, trajectory modification, DP

## V13 Nonformal Fixed-DP Candidate Expansion Retraining Execution

The predeclared non-formal fixed-DP candidate expansion and combined CAMP
retraining execution completed on AutoDL. The execution ran at CAMP commit
`24d4a5465cf11f0014de92465d3211d4bfc872cc` with DP fixed at
`7a1d33da277a1992ec474b5383a0c963c72e04e4`. It executed the 512 addon
fixed-DP replay commands, combined the addon selection logs with the completed
v13 base collection, built and validated the fallback-risk dataset, and trained
the static CAMP reranker with the predeclared simplex/CVaR/L2 objective.

This is a real CAMP retraining execution, but it is still an offline,
non-promotion artifact. CAMP did not generate, rewrite, blend, guide,
postprocess, or postselect trajectories. The trained weights only score the
fixed DP candidate set with `score_k(w)=a_k^T w`; DP remains the fixed black-box
candidate trajectory generator. The execution does not authorize promotion,
deployment, online selector changes, formal-seed use, DP modification, or any
safety/CAMP-over-DP Top-1 claim.

## V13 Candidate Expansion Retraining Post-Training Audits

The post-training nonpromotion artifact audit and development holdout
acceptance audit were executed on AutoDL after local, GitHub, and AutoDL CAMP
were synchronized at `4c522f61f4a2101bf81a3fda002f0d624ad70db7`. These audits
read only the newly trained fixed-DP candidate reranker artifacts from the
candidate-expansion combined retraining pipeline. They did not run replay,
generate candidates, train CAMP again, modify DP, promote atoms or selectors,
deploy, or make safety/CAMP-over-DP Top-1 claims.

nonnegative weights, JSON/NPY weight equality, strictly positive atom scales,
the approved 14-atom schema, and `score_k(w)=a_k^T w`. The development holdout
audit recomputed fixed-candidate validation-holdout scores over 5632 validation
records without feasible DP candidates; those metrics are diagnostic only and
are not safety or superiority claims.

## V13 Candidate Expansion Default-Off Shadow Selector Implementation

The candidate-expansion default-off shadow selector implementation gate was
validated after explicit user authorization for
`dp_camp_v13_default_off_shadow_selector_implementation_only_after_explicit_user_authorization`.
The production implementation already existed in the current runner and no
additional production diff was required in this gate. The validated
implementation is default-off and fail-closed: when enabled, the runner checks
the immutable artifact hash contract for atom scales and static
weights/checkpoint, computes CAMP scores over the fixed current-tick DP
candidate tensor, records `shadow_selected_index`, and forces `selected_index`
and `executed_index` to DP candidate 0. This implements shadow observability
only; it does not route CAMP selection into execution.

This gate did not run replay, generate candidates, train CAMP, modify DP,
promote atoms or selectors, deploy, change the online selector default, or
authorize safety/CAMP-over-DP claims.

## V13 Current-Source Default-Off Shadow Selector Static Contract Plan

The current-source default-off shadow selector static contract plan completed on
AutoDL at CAMP commit `897a07132d8ef4a88f67428440ba27cefbfbdcff` with fixed DP
commit `7a1d33da277a1992ec474b5383a0c963c72e04e4`. It consumed the
current-source promotion evidence package preflight and inspected the CAMP
integration source, replay runner source, and Benders atom contract test surface.

The plan is planning-only. It pins the static contract required before any
future implementation plan: a default-off shadow selector may only compute and
log a shadow index over the fixed current-tick K=8 DP candidate tensor using
`argmin_k score_k(w)` where `score_k(w)=a_k^T w`. Executed trajectory output
must remain DP Top-1, and fail-closed behavior must return DP Top-1 with no
shadow selection on missing artifacts, candidate-count drift, nonfinite values,
or source/hash mismatches. This plan does not implement, promote, deploy,
change the online selector, train CAMP, run replay, generate candidates, modify
DP, change executed trajectories, or authorize safety/CAMP-over-DP claims.

## Current V13 Current-Source Large-Data Default-Off Shadow Selector Static Contract Plan

The current-source large-data default-off shadow selector static contract plan
completed on AutoDL at CAMP commit
`5b6b465e343aaa51d2673740d1159cb4c3a7a61d` with fixed DP commit
`7a1d33da277a1992ec474b5383a0c963c72e04e4`. It consumed the current-source
large-data promotion evidence package preflight and inspected the CAMP
integration source, replay runner source, and Benders atom contract test
surface.

The plan is planning-only. It pins the static contract required before any
future implementation plan: a default-off shadow selector may only compute and
log a shadow index over the fixed current-tick K=8 DP candidate tensor using
`argmin_k score_k(w)` where `score_k(w)=a_k^T w`. Executed trajectory output
must remain DP Top-1, and fail-closed behavior must return DP Top-1 with no

## Current V13 Current-Source Large-Data Runtime Shadow Replay Preflight

The current-source large-data runtime shadow replay preflight inspected the
materialized runtime manifest, replay runner source/CLI contract, fixed DP
checkout, route, model, model args, replay config, reward config, non-formal
seed, planned output path, and fail-closed controls. It prepared one
default-off shadow replay smoke command for `sample_normal`, seed 301, `npc_0`,
`tl_off`, K=8. Seed 301 is not one of the frozen formal seeds 11/12/13. The
planned command uses fixed DP black-box candidate generation and runs CAMP only
as a default-off shadow reranker over the current-tick finite candidate set;
the executed trajectory must remain DP Top-1 and the shadow selector may only
log the shadow selected index and diagnostics.

This preflight wrote only reports and logs. It did not execute replay, generate
candidates, train CAMP, modify DP, promote atoms or selectors, deploy, change
online selection, change executed trajectories, or authorize
safety/CAMP-over-DP claims. It authorizes only the planned single non-formal
default-off shadow replay smoke execution as the next gate.

## Current V13 Current-Source Large-Data Runtime Shadow Replay Execution

The single non-formal default-off shadow replay smoke from the preflight was
executed against fixed DP commit `7a1d33da277a1992ec474b5383a0c963c72e04e4`
and CAMP commit `9598a87632f7ab0227be1168e893c12a487e1d88`. The first
execution attempt used the CAMP Python 3.9 environment and failed closed before
producing the planned replay output because the fixed DP import chain contains
Python 3.10+ union type syntax. That failed attempt did not train CAMP, modify
DP, promote, deploy, or create a usable replay artifact.

The same planned command was then executed with the AutoDL base Python 3.12
interpreter. It completed with exit code 0 and produced the planned
`camp_selection_log.json`, `camp_validation_summary.json`, and replay logs.
The static audit confirms that CAMP remained a default-off shadow reranker over
the fixed current-tick DP candidate tensor: executed and selected trajectories
stayed DP Top-1 for all 100 records, shadow scores were not routed to
execution, and the shadow-selected index was logged only as diagnostics.

This execution is evidence that the current-source large-data static CAMP
weights can be loaded into the runtime shadow path without changing DP Top-1
execution for the smoke case. It is not a safety benefit result, not a CAMP
over DP Top-1 result, not a selector promotion result, and not authorization to
modify DP or execute formal seeds.

batch preflight was materialized on AutoDL at CAMP commit
`c5c74e3d36b6e15fc4fd5839b8c504a9d0cb3127` with fixed DP commit
`7a1d33da277a1992ec474b5383a0c963c72e04e4`. It inspected the current runtime
manifest, runner source, v13 audit EOF, fixed DP checkout, model, model args,
reward config, route artifacts, static CAMP weights, and atom scales, then
wrote a JSON report, Markdown report, and a shell runbook. The runbook was not
executed by this gate.

The planned batch covers four routes (`sample_normal`, `sample_tl`,
`nishi_release`, `nishi_lane_change`), two non-formal seeds (301, 302), two NPC
settings (0, 4), and both traffic-light modes (`on`, `off`) for 100 replay
steps per command and K=8. The preflight verified that formal seeds 11/12/13
are excluded, all planned output paths are absent, output paths are unique, the
runtime manifest hash matches, the static weights and atom scales match the
manifest, all commands use the default-off shadow selector and runtime
manifest, no guidance/reference-blend/postselection/relaxation/splice flags are
present, and the runner contract still forces executed trajectories to DP
Top-1 while recording the shadow selected index.

This gate did not execute replay, generate candidates, train CAMP, modify DP,
promote selectors or atoms, deploy, change online selection, change executed
trajectories, or authorize safety/CAMP-over-DP claims.

## Current V13 Current-Source Large-Data Broader Shadow Replay Batch Execution

The broader non-formal current-source large-data default-off shadow replay
batch executed the 32 pinned runbook commands on AutoDL. The runbook was
executed with base Python 3.12 on CAMP commit
`c9b96ca29c11294bad3e3e8135c345811cd4b9bd` and fixed DP commit
`7a1d33da277a1992ec474b5383a0c963c72e04e4`. The non-interactive shell did not
provide a `python` executable by default, so the runbook was executed with
`PATH=/root/miniconda3/bin:$PATH`; the pinned runbook content was not edited.

The execution completed with exit code 0. The static batch audit found 32/32
selection logs, 32/32 validation summaries, 3200 selection records, and 3200
shadow records. Executed and selected indices remained DP Top-1 for every
record. The shadow reranker selected a nonzero candidate 2064 times, which
confirms the shadow scoring path was live while never routing shadow scores to
execution. The static audit also confirmed that reference blending, guidance,
closed-loop outcome inputs, CAMP-generated candidates, DP modification, CAMP
training, selector/atom promotion, deployment, and safety/CAMP-over-DP claims
were not part of this gate.

## V13 Current-Source Large-Data Broader Shadow Replay Batch Training Readiness Review

The read-only training-readiness review was implemented and run against the
fixed AutoDL broader shadow replay batch. The review did not run replay,
generate candidates, train CAMP, modify DP, promote selectors or atoms, deploy,
or authorize safety/CAMP-over-DP claims. It inspected only the fixed replay
output, execution artifact, static batch audit, and existing training data
contract.

The replay data is materially usable as a DP-reward labeled fixed-candidate
source: 32 selection logs contain 3200 records, 2651 records have at least one
feasible fixed DP candidate, 2610 records have at least two feasible fixed DP
candidates, and 549 all-infeasible records would be dropped by the current
static DP-reward training script before fitting. Candidate count is 8 for all
records, atom schema is `dp_camp_v10_14d` for all records, DP reward labels are
present for all records, and closed-loop outcome labels are absent for all
records.

The review correctly fails closed before training because the existing clean
training-data contract validator requires `camp_candidate_tensor_provenance` to
be a dict. This v13 default-off shadow artifact instead logs the fixed tensor
provenance under `default_off_shadow_selector`. All 3200 records have valid
`default_off_shadow_selector` payloads, but all 3200 records have missing legacy
`camp_candidate_tensor_provenance` dict payloads. Therefore the next admissible
gate is a narrow training-data-contract remediation only, not CAMP retraining.

## V13 Default-Off Shadow Training Data Contract Remediation

The default-off shadow training-data contract remediation was implemented and
validated on the fixed broader non-formal current-source large replay batch.
The clean DP-native training-data contract now accepts either the legacy
`camp_candidate_tensor_provenance` payload or the v13
`default_off_shadow_selector` provenance payload, but only when the v13 payload
strictly proves default-off behavior, DP Top-1 execution, fixed DP candidate
reranking, affine scoring, no online selector effect, no DP modification, and a
valid fixed candidate tensor hash. The legacy contract remains supported and
the validator still fails closed on guidance, reference blending, DP weight
changes, tensor mutation, trajectory rewrite, and closed-loop outcome input
leaks.

The fixed AutoDL replay artifact now passes the clean contract validator: 32
selection logs, 3200 records, and 0 failed records. The training-readiness
review also passes under the current remediation EOF, with 2651 records
available for static DP-reward feasible-ranking training and 549 all-infeasible
records that the existing static training script will drop before fitting.
This gate did not run replay, generate candidates, train CAMP, modify DP,
promote selectors or atoms, deploy, or authorize safety/CAMP-over-DP claims.

## V13 Static DP-Reward Training Execution

The static DP-reward CAMP training gate was executed on AutoDL using only the
fixed broader non-formal current-source large shadow replay selection logs. The
training command required the clean DP-native training-data contract and the
approved atom schema. It used `label_source=dp_reward`,
`reward_key=quality_without_progress`, and `reward_progress_weight=2.0`.

The training script loaded 3200 fixed-DP candidate records, dropped the 549
records without any feasible candidate as designed by the existing static
training implementation, and trained on 2651 records. The output weights are
finite, nonnegative, length 14, and sum to 1 within numerical tolerance. The
atom scales are finite positive length-14 values under `dp_camp_v10_14d`.
This is a non-promotion static training artifact only. The observed
`oracle_match_rate=0.15918521312712183` is recorded as training diagnostics
only and is not a safety, deployment, or CAMP-over-DP claim.

This gate did not run replay, generate new candidates, modify DP, use formal
seeds 11/12/13, use closed-loop outcome or SafetyCost labels, promote selectors
or atoms, deploy, or authorize safety/CAMP-over-DP claims.

## V13 Static DP-Reward Training Artifact Shadow Replay Evaluation Preflight

The trained-artifact shadow replay/evaluation preflight gate was executed on
AutoDL using only the fixed static DP-reward training artifact from the previous
gate. The first preflight attempt used stale local route/config paths and was
rejected before any runtime manifest was written. The accepted rerun used the
existing fixed AutoDL assets under `/root/autodl-tmp/camp_dp_assets` and the
script's current underscore-style CLI contract.

The accepted preflight materialized a non-promotion runtime artifact manifest
and a runbook for a future default-off shadow replay/evaluation pass. It planned
32 commands across the four fixed non-formal routes, seeds 301/302, NPC counts
0/4, traffic lights on/off, 100 steps, and K=8, for an expected 3200 records.
The manifest keeps `selection_effect=false` and `executed_output_policy=dp_top1`;
the planned commands use fixed DP candidate generation and only add CAMP as a
default-off shadow selector over fixed DP candidates.

This gate did not execute replay, generate candidates, modify DP, use formal
seeds 11/12/13, promote selectors or atoms, deploy, change online selection,
change executed trajectories, or authorize safety/CAMP-over-DP claims.

## V13 Static DP-Reward Training Artifact Shadow Replay Evaluation Execution

The trained-artifact shadow replay/evaluation execution gate was run on AutoDL
from the fixed preflight runbook. The initial execution attempt used the older
`camp` Python 3.9 environment and failed before creating replay outputs because
the fixed Diffusion Planner code imports Python 3.10+ union type syntax in
`guidance_gui/generate_samples.py`. No `camp_selection_log.json` outputs were
created by that failed attempt. The accepted rerun used the existing
`/root/autodl-tmp/dp312_venv` Python 3.12 environment with `PYTHONPATH` pointing
at the fixed CAMP and Diffusion Planner source trees; no DP files, weights, or
configs were modified.

The accepted execution completed the 32 planned non-formal default-off shadow
replay/evaluation commands: four fixed routes, seeds 301/302, NPC counts 0/4,
traffic lights on/off, 100 steps, and K=8. It produced 32
`camp_selection_log.json` files and 3200 records. Each route produced eight
logs. The runbook kept DP Top-1 as the executed output while logging CAMP's
static DP-reward artifact choice as a default-off shadow selector.

A read-only execution audit was added and run on AutoDL. The audit passed:
default-off selector contract violations were zero, executed-index violations
were zero, reference-blend/guidance/postselection/closed-loop-outcome violations
were zero, atom-schema violations were zero, and affine raw-score violations
were zero. The 597 non-finite `selection_scores` entries were verified as
infeasible-candidate `inf` masks; raw `scores` remained affine in the logged
weights and normalized atoms with maximum error
`8.881784197001252e-16`.

This gate did not modify DP, did not train CAMP, did not use formal seeds
11/12/13, did not promote selectors or atoms, did not deploy, did not change
online selection, did not change executed trajectories, and does not authorize
any safety or CAMP-over-DP claim.

Completed the EOF-authorized static preflight for evaluating the fixed broader
non-formal static DP-reward training artifact in default-off shadow replay. The
preflight consumed the fixed training summary, atom scales, and learned weights
from the 763a80b training artifact, verified the current CAMP/GitHub and fixed
DP heads, verified the `dp_camp_v10_14d` atom schema and 14-dimensional simplex
weights, wrote a default-off runtime manifest for the trained weights/scales,
and generated a non-executed 32-command shadow replay/evaluation runbook.

The planned evaluation scope mirrors the broader non-formal batch shape:
routes `sample_normal`, `sample_tl`, `nishi_release`, and
`nishi_lane_change`; seeds `301,302`; traffic lights `on,off`; max NPC values
`0,4`; 100 steps per run; and K=8 fixed DP candidates. The preflight expects
3200 future records if the next gate executes. The runbook uses only fixed DP
candidate generation plus CAMP default-off shadow reranking, with the executed
output policy pinned to DP Top-1.

This gate did not execute replay, generate candidates, train CAMP, modify DP,
use formal seeds 11/12/13, use reference_blend, guidance,

selectors or atoms, deploy, or authorize safety/CAMP-over-DP claims.

## Current V13 Current-Source Large Broader Static DP-Reward Artifact Shadow Replay Evaluation Execution After f6fcc7e

Date: 2026-06-29

Completed the EOF-authorized static DP-reward artifact shadow replay/evaluation
execution gate over the fixed broader non-formal runbook. The first execution
attempt used the preflight runbook's `camp` Python 3.9 interpreter and failed
before producing replay outputs because fixed Diffusion-Planner imports require
Python 3.10+ union type syntax. No replay logs were produced by that failed
attempt.

The remediation rerun changed only the Python executable in the generated
runbook to the existing `/root/autodl-tmp/dp312_venv/bin/python` interpreter.
It did not change DP source/config/weights, CAMP code, routes, seeds, model
artifacts, static weights/scales, runtime manifest, candidate flags, or output
policy. The rerun executed all 32 planned default-off shadow replay commands,
produced 32 `camp_selection_log.json` files and 3200 records, and the read-only
execution audit passed.

This gate executed fixed DP candidate generation as part of the authorized
non-formal replay/evaluation, while CAMP remained a default-off shadow
reranker: the executed policy stayed DP Top-1. It did not train CAMP, modify
DP, use formal seeds 11/12/13, use reference_blend, guidance,
postprocess/postselection, collect/read closed-loop outcomes, promote selectors
or atoms, deploy, or authorize safety/CAMP-over-DP claims.

`7a1d33da277a1992ec474b5383a0c963c72e04e4`. The later read-only audit ran on
CAMP commit `b383320d1009220c44e796e9f45afdee48b9233d` after the audit script
was minimally parameterized to record a separate execution artifact HEAD,
accept the wrapper's `stdout.log`/`stderr.log`/`SHA256SUMS` names, and override
the next gate string without changing old defaults.

The execution artifact has `runbook.exit=0`. The audit artifact has
`audit.exit=0`, `failed_checks=[]`, 32 `camp_selection_log.json` files, and
3200 records. Every selection log has exactly 100 records. `selected_index` and
`executed_index` remained DP Top-1 (`0`) for all 3200 records. CAMP's
default-off shadow selector selected a nonzero candidate in 3061 records, which
shows the shadow scorer was live, but those shadow choices were not routed to
execution. The audit found zero default-off contract, executed-index,
postselection, reference-blend, guidance, closed-loop-outcome, atom-schema,
shape, affine-score, or selection-score-mask violations. The 597 non-finite
selection scores were valid infeasible-candidate `inf` masks; raw scores
remained affine in the logged atom features and weights with maximum error
`8.881784197001252e-16`.

This gate used fixed DP as the black-box candidate trajectory generator and
used CAMP only to rerank the fixed DP candidate tensor in default-off shadow
mode. It did not train CAMP, modify DP, use formal seeds 11/12/13, use
reference blending, guidance, postprocess/postselection, closed-loop outcome
inputs, promote selectors or atoms, deploy, change online selection, change
executed trajectories, or authorize safety/CAMP-over-DP claims.

## Current V13 Static DP-Reward Eval Plus Prior Shadow Replay Result Review Rejected After 7631f78

The read-only result review gate for the static DP-reward eval-plus-prior
shadow replay/evaluation artifact was run on AutoDL and rejected the result as
not admissible for the next training-preflight gate. The clean execution
contract still held: 32 selection logs, 3200 records, fixed DP Top-1 execution
for all records, CAMP default-off shadow reranking only, no DP modification,
zero formal seed 11/12/13 records, no reference blend, guidance,
postselection, closed-loop outcome input, CAMP candidate generation, or
trajectory modification. The rejection was specifically caused by candidate
tensor overlap against the prior training summary selection logs:
`eval_hashes_in_previous_rate=1.0`, meaning all 3200 current evaluation
candidate tensors were already present in the prior training evidence source.

This gate did not train CAMP, replay, generate candidates, modify DP, promote
selectors or atoms, deploy, change online selection, change executed
trajectories, or authorize safety/CAMP-over-DP claims. Because the result
review failed, no training preflight, training execution, replay execution,
promotion, deployment, or selector change is authorized by this section.

## Current V13 Static DP-Reward Eval Plus Prior Non-Overlap Data Remediation Plan After 6ffbd21

The plan-only non-overlap data remediation gate completed on AutoDL after the
overlap failure diagnosis. The plan accepts the diagnosis that the current
evaluation artifact is not an independent holdout and defines the remediation
contracts required before any future training-preflight gate: an explicit split
manifest, candidate-tensor hash registry, path-signature registry,
record-identity hash registry, zero train/eval candidate-tensor intersection,
zero train/eval path-signature intersection, and result-readiness comparison
against all `training_summary.selection_logs`. It also requires any later
holdout source root to be distinct from the diagnosed prior evaluation root and
from all training-summary selection logs.

This gate did not train CAMP, replay, generate candidates, modify DP, promote
selectors or atoms, deploy, change online selection, change executed
trajectories, or authorize safety/CAMP-over-DP claims. It authorizes only a
static contract review of this remediation plan. It does not authorize training
preflight, training execution, replay execution, candidate generation, fixed-DP
candidate collection execution, promotion, deployment, or selector change.

completed on AutoDL. The review consumed only the prior plan JSON and the v13
audit, verified that the plan keeps CAMP as a fixed-DP-candidate reranker, and
confirmed that the required non-overlap contracts are pinned before any later
implementation-plan gate: split manifest, candidate-tensor hash registry,
path-signature registry, record-identity hash registry, zero train/eval
candidate-tensor intersection, zero train/eval path-signature intersection,
and result-readiness comparison against all `training_summary.selection_logs`.

AutoDL direct GitHub fetch timed out while syncing the review script, so this
checkpoint was synced to AutoDL with a git bundle after the commit was pushed to
GitHub. After the bundle sync, AutoDL CAMP `HEAD` and `origin/main` both matched
the pushed commit. DP remained fixed at
`7a1d33da277a1992ec474b5383a0c963c72e04e4`.

This gate did not train CAMP, replay, generate candidates, modify DP, promote
selectors or atoms, deploy, change online selection, change executed
trajectories, or authorize safety/CAMP-over-DP claims. It authorizes only a
future implementation-plan gate. It does not authorize implementation,
training preflight, training execution, replay execution, candidate generation,
fixed-DP candidate collection execution, promotion, deployment, or selector
change.

## Current V13 Static DP-Reward Eval Plus Prior Non-Overlap Data Remediation Implementation Plan After 9f3af49

The plan-only implementation-plan gate completed on AutoDL. The plan consumed
the completed non-overlap static contract review and the current result-readiness
script, then defined the future implementation scope required to prevent train
and holdout overlap before any later training-preflight gate. The planned future
work is limited to adding structured split/registry inputs and non-overlap
validation to the result-readiness surface: split manifest, candidate-tensor
hash registry, path-signature registry, record-identity hash registry, zero
train/eval candidate-tensor intersection, zero train/eval path-signature
intersection, zero train/eval record-identity intersection, comparison against
all `training_summary.selection_logs`, and formal-seed exclusion.

This gate did not implement result-readiness changes, build a split manifest,
run replay, generate candidates, train CAMP, modify DP, promote selectors or
atoms, deploy, change online selection, change executed trajectories, or
authorize safety/CAMP-over-DP claims. It authorizes only a future static
contract review of the implementation plan. It does not authorize
implementation, training preflight, training execution, replay execution,
candidate generation, fixed-DP candidate collection execution, promotion,
deployment, or selector change.

## Current V13 Static DP-Reward Eval Plus Prior Non-Overlap Data Remediation Implementation Static Contract Review After ccfb8841

The read-only implementation static contract review completed on AutoDL after
one rejected attempt exposed an over-strict source-surface check in the new
review script. The rejected attempt did not train CAMP, replay, generate
candidates, modify DP, promote, deploy, or change any selector behavior. Its
failed checks were limited to source literal checks against the implementation
plan script. The check was corrected in `ccfb8841` to match stable gate
fragments in source text rather than fully concatenated runtime constants, and
the real review then passed.

The passing review consumed the implementation-plan JSON, the implementation
plan script/test, the current result-readiness script, and this v13 audit. It
confirmed that the future implementation scope remains limited to adding
structured non-overlap inputs and validation to result-readiness. The review
authorizes only the next implementation gate. It does not authorize training
preflight, training execution, replay execution, fixed-DP candidate generation,
CAMP candidate generation, trajectory generation or modification, DP
modification, selector or atom promotion, deployment, deployable checkpoint
claims, safety benefit claims, or CAMP-over-DP Top-1 claims.

The mathematical and integration boundary remains unchanged: CAMP is a
default-off shadow reranker over fixed DP candidate tensors only; the executed
trajectory remains DP Top-1; `score_k(w)=a_k^T w`; only approved atoms with
nonnegative simplex weights are in scope; simplex/CVaR/L2 master convexity must
be preserved; formal seeds 11/12/13 remain forbidden.

## Current V13 Static DP-Reward Eval Plus Prior Non-Overlap Data Remediation Implementation After 8827ed93

The implementation-only gate completed on local Windows and AutoDL. The only
production-surface change was to the read-only result-readiness reviewer: it now
accepts explicit structured non-overlap evidence for the split manifest,
candidate tensor hash registry, path signature registry, and record identity
hash registry. The target tests add happy-path and rejection coverage for
train/holdout split overlap, formal seed use, candidate tensor registry overlap,
path signature overlap, and record identity overlap.

This gate did not train CAMP, run replay, generate candidates, modify DP,
promote selectors or atoms, deploy, change online selector behavior, or make any
safety or CAMP-over-DP Top-1 claim. CAMP remains a default-off shadow reranker
over fixed DP candidate tensors only. `score_k(w)=a_k^T w` remains the scoring
contract; only approved atoms with nonnegative simplex weights are in scope; the
simplex/CVaR/L2 master remains convex; formal seeds 11/12/13 remain forbidden.

## Current V13 Static DP-Reward Eval Plus Prior Non-Overlap Data Remediation Post-Implementation Static Contract Review After 2ab929c0

The post-implementation static contract review completed on local Windows and
AutoDL. This gate added a read-only reviewer for the implemented non-overlap
result-readiness hardening and then executed it on AutoDL against the current
implementation artifact, result-readiness source/test, v13 audit, and fixed
HEAD evidence.

The review confirmed that result-readiness now requires explicit structured
split/registry evidence, checks train/eval intersections for candidate tensors,
path signatures, and record identities, rejects formal seeds 11/12/13, and
preserves the prior-training candidate-tensor hash comparison. It authorizes
only the next read-only result-review gate. It does not authorize training
preflight, training execution, replay execution, fixed-DP candidate generation,
CAMP candidate generation, trajectory generation or modification, DP
modification, selector or atom promotion, deployment, deployable checkpoint
claims, safety benefit claims, or CAMP-over-DP Top-1 claims.

The mathematical and integration boundary remains unchanged: CAMP is a
default-off shadow reranker over fixed DP candidate tensors only; the executed
trajectory remains DP Top-1; `score_k(w)=a_k^T w`; only approved atoms with
nonnegative simplex weights are in scope; simplex/CVaR/L2 master convexity must
be preserved; formal seeds 11/12/13 remain forbidden.

## Current V13 Static DP-Reward Eval Plus Prior Result Review Rejected By Non-Overlap Registries After fcd4e6ad

The read-only result review was re-run on AutoDL after the non-overlap
result-readiness hardening landed. This gate did not replay, generate
candidates, train CAMP, modify DP, promote, deploy, or make safety/CAMP-over-DP
claims. It only derived structured split/registry evidence from existing
evaluation selection logs and the prior training summary, then passed those
read-only inputs into the current result-readiness reviewer.

The review correctly rejected the artifact. The current evaluation still
overlaps the prior training artifact: the derived candidate tensor registry has
2,180 unique candidate tensor hashes in common; the path signature registry has
32 route/seed/npc/spawn/tl/static-shadow signatures in common; and the record
identity registry has all 3,200 evaluation records in common. The older
candidate tensor overlap guard also failed. This confirms the remediation
implementation is active and blocks training-preflight on overlapping
evaluation data.

The rejection is a data split/remediation issue, not evidence of DP modification
or CAMP trajectory generation. CAMP remains a default-off shadow reranker over
fixed DP candidate tensors only; executed trajectory remains DP Top-1;
`score_k(w)=a_k^T w`; only approved atoms with nonnegative simplex weights are
in scope; simplex/CVaR/L2 master convexity remains preserved; formal seeds
11/12/13 remain forbidden.

## Current V13 Static DP-Reward Eval Plus Prior Non-Overlap Holdout Data Preparation Plan After 3a00bc94

The non-overlap holdout data preparation plan-only gate completed on local
Windows and AutoDL. This gate consumed the rejected result-readiness artifact
from the overlapping evaluation and planned the next independent holdout data
preparation contract. It did not prepare data, run replay, generate fixed-DP
candidates, train CAMP, modify DP, promote selectors or atoms, deploy, or make
safety/CAMP-over-DP Top-1 claims.

An earlier plan artifact on 7c2ffb17 rejected because the first script version
expected candidate/atom count values as lists, while the real result-readiness
artifact reports count distributions (`{"8": 3200}` and `{"14": 3200}`). That
script-contract issue did not execute replay, training, candidate generation, or
DP modification. The 3a00bc94 revision accepts count distributions and the
current artifact passed.

The plan targets a larger future non-overlap holdout set: minimum 32 selection
logs / 3,200 records, target 128 selection logs / 12,800 records, 100 steps per
log, 8 fixed-DP candidates, and 14 approved atoms. The future holdout must
exclude prior-training roots/signatures/record identities and the rejected
evaluation roots/signatures/record identities; all candidate tensor, path
signature, and record identity intersections must be zero before any training
preflight. Formal seeds 11/12/13 remain forbidden. CAMP remains a default-off
shadow reranker over fixed DP candidate tensors only; `score_k(w)=a_k^T w`;
approved atoms with nonnegative simplex weights only; simplex/CVaR/L2 master
convexity preserved.

## Current V13 Static DP-Reward Eval Plus Prior Non-Overlap Holdout Data Preparation Implementation Static Contract Review After cd48eef5

The read-only implementation static contract review for non-overlap holdout
data preparation completed on local Windows and AutoDL. This gate reviewed the
faa258dd implementation-plan artifact, the implementation-plan script/test, the
current v13 audit, and fixed HEAD evidence. It did not implement the builder,
prepare data, run fixed-DP candidate generation, run replay, train CAMP, modify
DP, promote selectors or atoms, deploy, or make safety/CAMP-over-DP Top-1
claims.

The first real review artifact at 4167e2d0 rejected because the review script
over-required exact source text that the real implementation-plan script stored
through constants and split string literals, and because the real implementation
plan tests used longer test names than the initial review expected. This was a
static review source-contract issue, not a data, DP, or CAMP behavior issue. The
review contract was narrowed to check the actual equivalent source evidence and
then passed at cd48eef5.

The passing review authorizes only a future manifest-builder implementation:
materialize `holdout_candidate_request_manifest.json`,
`nonoverlap_exclusion_registry_manifest.json`, `holdout_preparation_runbook.sh`,
`expected_holdout_artifact_manifest.json`, and SHA256SUMS. It still does not
authorize data preparation, fixed-DP candidate generation, replay, training,
selector or atom promotion, deployment, or claims. CAMP remains fixed-DP
candidate reranking only with `score_k(w)=a_k^T w`; approved atoms with
nonnegative simplex weights only; simplex/CVaR/L2 master convexity preserved.

The manifest-only non-overlap holdout data preparation builder completed on
local Windows and AutoDL. This gate implemented and executed only a
default-off manifest builder. It materialized a non-formal route/seed request
manifest, exclusion-registry manifest, validation runbook, expected artifact
manifest, and SHA256SUMS. It did not prepare data, run fixed-DP candidate
generation, run replay, train CAMP, modify DP, promote selectors or atoms,

the source authorization, the prior training summary artifact as the training
registry reference, and the rejected fcd4e6ad result-readiness artifact as the
overlap-exclusion reference. The generated holdout request manifest contains

## Current V13 Static DP-Reward Eval Plus Prior Non-Overlap Holdout Manifest Builder Post-Implementation Static Contract Review After 343c46ee

The manifest builder post-implementation static contract review completed on
local Windows and AutoDL. This gate was read-only with respect to DP/CAMP data
execution: it inspected the current builder source, builder tests, v13 audit EOF,
and the previously materialized 52127d36 manifest builder artifact. It did not
prepare data, run fixed-DP candidate generation, run replay, train CAMP, modify
DP, promote selectors or atoms, deploy, or make safety/CAMP-over-DP Top-1
claims.

One first AutoDL execution attempt is retained as a failed attempt artifact:
the runbook's source-artifact glob selected a prior post-review directory rather
than the intended 52127d36 manifest-builder artifact. That failure is attributed
to runbook source selection, not to the static contract. The rerun used the
exact 52127d36 manifest-builder artifact path and passed with 133 checks.

The passed review authorizes only the next non-formal holdout data-preparation
gate using fixed DP candidate generation from the existing manifest request set.
CAMP remains fixed-DP candidate reranking only with `score_k(w)=a_k^T w`;
approved atoms with nonnegative simplex weights only; simplex/CVaR/L2 master
convexity preserved. CAMP candidate generation, trajectory generation,
trajectory modification, DP modification, replay, training, promotion,
deployment, and safety/CAMP-over-DP claims remain unauthorized by this gate.

## Current V13 Static DP-Reward Eval Plus Prior Non-Overlap Holdout Data-Preparation Execution Audit After 78ee139a

The non-formal holdout data-preparation execution completed and was audited
with a read-only post-execution audit. The source data-preparation artifact was
generated at CAMP source head d5350de824c55ff122d670395013642e2dcc6b9a using
the fixed DP commit 7a1d33da277a1992ec474b5383a0c963c72e04e4. It materialized
128 default-off shadow selection logs and 12,800 records from fixed DP
candidate generation. The audit code itself ran at a later CAMP audit head
78ee139aae00e4a8a20ec192fae9b92249b1e677; this is recorded separately from
the source artifact head.

Two earlier data-preparation execution attempts are retained as rejected
attempts. The first used the CAMP Python 3.9 environment to invoke DP source
that requires Python 3.10+ union syntax, causing a DP import/runtime type-error
before any data was prepared. The second used Python 3.12 but did not pass
`--camp_atom_scales` and `--camp_static_weights` into the replay runner, so it
did not materialize CAMP selection logs and was stopped without promotion or
data acceptance. A first execution-audit attempt at f8be19e9 is also retained
as rejected: it incorrectly required the source artifact CAMP head and the
audit-tool CAMP head to be identical. That audit contract was corrected to
record both heads and require source internal consistency plus fixed DP.

The passed execution audit found no data-contract failures: commands completed
128/128, failed commands were empty, selection logs were 128/128, records were
12,800/12,800, DP Top-1 executed-index violations were zero, missing shadow
indices were zero, formal seed 11/12/13 records were zero, registry counts
matched 12,800 candidate tensor hashes, 128 path signatures, and 12,800 record
identity hashes, and the future training data contract passed. The audit also
records two source-artifact evidence warnings rather than hiding them: the
ad-hoc launcher did not write a raw `run_data_preparation.exit`, and the source
artifact's original `SHA256SUMS` no longer verifies post-execution because it
hashed `execution.stdout.txt` before the wrapper finished writing the final
stdout JSON. The audit artifact includes an independent post-execution source
SHA manifest and its own exit/log/SHA evidence.

CAMP remains fixed-DP candidate reranking only with `score_k(w)=a_k^T w`;
approved atoms with nonnegative simplex weights only; simplex/CVaR/L2 master
convexity preserved. The source execution performed fixed DP candidate
generation for data preparation only. It did not train CAMP, run replay
evaluation, modify DP, promote selectors or atoms, deploy, or make
safety/CAMP-over-DP Top-1 claims. The only authorized next work is the
non-overlap holdout static DP-reward training preflight.

## Current V13 Static DP-Reward Eval Plus Prior Non-Overlap Holdout Training Preflight After 7c57be5a

The non-overlap holdout static DP-reward training preflight completed on
AutoDL at CAMP head 7c57be5a434be005480d326f5e5751e3bea2cade with the fixed
DP commit 7a1d33da277a1992ec474b5383a0c963c72e04e4. This gate only validated
the prior plus holdout default-off shadow selection logs and materialized a
selection manifest, training command plan, and runbook. It did not execute
training, replay, DP candidate generation, CAMP candidate generation,
trajectory generation, trajectory modification, promotion, deployment, or any
safety/CAMP-over-DP claim.

The preflight accepted 32 prior logs and 128 non-overlap holdout logs, for 160
selection logs and 16,000 total records. The future training-data contract
passed with 0 failed records, 13,616 usable feasible records, 0 formal
seed 11/12/13 records, 0 prior-vs-holdout candidate tensor overlap, 0 guidance
records, 0 reference-blend records, 0 postselection records, 0 closed-loop
outcome records, 0 CAMP candidate-generation effect records, and 0 DP
modification records. The planned command remains static DP-reward training
over fixed DP candidate tensors with `--label_source dp_reward`,
`--reward_key quality_without_progress`, `--reward_progress_weight 2.0`,
`--require_dp_native_training_data_contract`, and `--require_atom_schema`.

CAMP remains fixed-DP candidate reranking only with `score_k(w)=a_k^T w`.
The planned training command is limited to approved atoms with nonnegative
simplex weights and preserves simplex/CVaR/L2 master convexity. The only
authorized next work is non-overlap holdout static DP-reward training
execution. Replay evaluation, promotion, deployment, DP modification, CAMP
candidate generation, CAMP trajectory generation, CAMP trajectory
modification, and safety/CAMP-over-DP claims remain unauthorized.

## Current V13 Static DP-Reward Eval Plus Prior Non-Overlap Holdout Training Execution Audit After f972030f

The non-overlap holdout static DP-reward training execution completed on
AutoDL from the preflighted runbook. The source training execution ran at CAMP
head 2050aa78d506477b79306a4bd731e8595881bbb2 with DP fixed at
7a1d33da277a1992ec474b5383a0c963c72e04e4. The read-only training execution
audit ran later at CAMP audit head f972030f034254a5775da16193a3fd5eb3ccf6a3,
recording the source execution head separately from the audit-tool head.

Training consumed the preflighted 160 fixed-DP default-off shadow selection
logs and the DP-native training-data contract records=16,000. The trainer used
13,616 records with at least one feasible candidate and dropped 2,384 records
without any feasible candidate. It wrote only the static training artifacts:
`training_summary.json`, `offline_weights_dp_static.npy`, and
`atom_scales_dp_static.json`. No replay, DP candidate generation, CAMP
candidate generation, trajectory generation, trajectory modification, DP
modification, promotion, deployment, or safety/CAMP-over-DP claim occurred.

The learned static weights are finite, nonnegative, 14-dimensional, and sum to
1.0000000000000002, satisfying the simplex contract within tolerance. The atom
scales use schema dp_camp_v10_14d, contain 14 strictly positive scales, and the
score boundary remains `score_k(w)=a_k^T w`. The training summary caveat is
preserved: candidate-level DP rewards are model-based preferences, not
counterfactual closed-loop outcomes. The only authorized next work is a
training-artifact shadow replay/evaluation preflight; replay execution,
promotion, deployment, DP modification, CAMP candidate generation, CAMP
trajectory generation/modification, and safety/CAMP-over-DP claims remain
unauthorized.

## Current V13 Static DP-Reward Eval Plus Prior Non-Overlap Holdout Training Artifact Shadow Replay Evaluation Python312 Preflight After 797cecf

Date: 2026-06-30

Completed the EOF-authorized preflight for evaluating the non-overlap holdout
static DP-reward training artifact in default-off shadow replay. This gate
consumed the fixed non-overlap holdout training summary, learned simplex
weights, and atom scales, then wrote a new default-off runtime manifest and a
non-executed Python 3.12 replay runbook. It selected fresh non-formal seeds
`1200,1201`, which were absent from the training summary seed paths before the
preflight, to avoid repeating the prior overlap failure pattern.

The planned evaluation scope covers routes `sample_normal`, `sample_tl`,
`nishi_release`, and `nishi_lane_change`; seeds `1200,1201`; max NPC values
`0,4`; traffic lights `on,off`; 100 steps per command; and K=8 fixed DP
candidates. The preflight produced 32 planned commands and expects 3200 future
records if the next execution-only gate runs. The runtime manifest remains
default-off with `selection_effect=False` and `executed_output_policy=dp_top1`.

This preflight did not execute replay, generate candidates, train CAMP, modify
DP, use formal seeds 11/12/13, use reference_blend, guidance,
postprocess/postselection, collect or read closed-loop outcomes, promote
selectors or atoms, deploy, or authorize safety/CAMP-over-DP claims. The next
gate is limited to Python 3.12 default-off shadow replay/evaluation execution
for the fixed DP candidate generator and fixed CAMP reranker artifacts.

## Current V13 Static DP-Reward Eval Plus Prior Non-Overlap Holdout Training Artifact Shadow Replay Evaluation Training Preflight After daa4d5e

Date: 2026-06-30

Completed the EOF-authorized static DP-reward training preflight over fixed
artifacts only. The preflight used the prior non-overlap holdout training
selection manifest as the fixed prior input and the latest non-overlap holdout
training-artifact shadow replay evaluation logs as the fixed evaluation input.
No training, replay execution, candidate generation, DP modification,
reference_blend, guidance, postprocess/postselection, closed-loop outcome
collection, selector/atom promotion, deployment, safety claim, or CAMP-over-DP
claim was executed by this gate.

The preflight passed and materialized only a selection-log manifest, static
DP-reward training command plan, and a runbook for a later execution gate. The
combined fixed input contains 192 selection logs and 19,200 records: 16,000
prior records plus 3,200 evaluation records. It has 16,482 records with at
least one feasible candidate, 2,718 all-infeasible records that static
training will drop, zero formal-seed records, zero reference_blend records,
zero guidance records, zero postselection records, zero closed-loop outcome
records, zero CAMP candidate-generation-effect records, and zero DP
modification records. Prior/evaluation candidate tensor overlap remains zero.

The planned command remains static DP-reward training over fixed DP candidate
tensors with `--label_source dp_reward`, `--reward_key
quality_without_progress`, `--reward_progress_weight 2.0`,
`--require_dp_native_training_data_contract`, and `--require_atom_schema`. CAMP
remains fixed-DP candidate reranking only with `score_k(w)=a_k^T w`; the
planned training uses approved atoms with nonnegative simplex weights and
preserves simplex/CVaR/L2 master convexity. The only authorized next work is
the corresponding static DP-reward training execution gate; replay evaluation,
candidate generation, DP modification, promotion, deployment, and safety or
CAMP-over-DP claims remain unauthorized.
